root_cause.text: In the AMD display HDCP2 HDMI repeater path, mod_hdcp_read_rx_id_list() trusted the unvalidated 10-bit RxStatus-derived rx_id_list_size as the I2C read length for the fixed-size hdcp->auth.msg.hdcp2.rx_id_list buffer, allowing an out-of-bounds write.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit states the HDMI code used the sink-advertised message size “without being clamped to the size of the destination buffer rx_id_list[177]” and the patch fixes this by changing the read length from hdcp->auth.msg.hdcp2.rx_id_list_size to MIN(hdcp->auth.msg.hdcp2.rx_id_list_size, sizeof(hdcp->auth.msg.hdcp2.rx_id_list)).

agent_logs.evidence_points: The CVE/commit states the HDMI code used the sink-advertised message size “without being clamped to the size of the destination buffer rx_id_list[177]” and the patch fixes this by changing the read length from hdcp->auth.msg.hdcp2.rx_id_list_size to MIN(hdcp->auth.msg.hdcp2.rx_id_list_size, sizeof(hdcp->auth.msg.hdcp2.rx_id_list)).

intent_record.intent_summary: Clamp the HDCP receiver ID list read size to the destination buffer length to prevent overflow.
intent_record.what: The call to read() in mod_hdcp_read_rx_id_list() was changed so that the length argument is no longer hdcp->auth.msg.hdcp2.rx_id_list_size directly, but instead MIN(hdcp->auth.msg.hdcp2.rx_id_list_size, sizeof(hdcp->auth.msg.hdcp2.rx_id_list)).
intent_record.how: This limits the number of bytes read into hdcp->auth.msg.hdcp2.rx_id_list to the actual size of the destination buffer, preventing an oversized rx_id_list_size from causing a buffer overflow during runtime.

grouping_result.intent: Clamp the HDCP receiver ID list read size to the destination buffer length to prevent overflow.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly addresses the root cause by validating/clamping the RxStatus-derived receiver ID list read length to the fixed destination buffer size, preventing the out-of-bounds write in mod_hdcp_read_rx_id_list().

candidates.rationale: This unvalidated RxStatus-derived size is passed directly as the read length for filling the fixed-size rx_id_list buffer, enabling an out-of-bounds write if the size exceeds the buffer capacity.
This is the vulnerable read operation that uses the attacker-influenced rx_id_list_size as its transfer length, causing the overflow into the destination buffer.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the read operation that initiates filling the fixed-size hdcp->auth.msg.hdcp2.rx_id_list buffer using the unvalidated RxStatus-derived size, leading to the out-of-bounds write.
This line supplies the attacker-influenced rx_id_list_size directly as the read length without bounds checking against the destination buffer size, which is the root cause of the overflow.
